description: Turns the chord arriving on an MPX stream into an arpeggio, playing its tones one at a time in time with the chart

params.text: Sets how often a note falls: once a bar, once in two beats, once a beat, or two, three or four a beat
Sets the order the tones are played in: up, down, up and down, random, or all at once as a chord
Sets how many octaves the figure climbs through before it starts again, one, two or three
Chooses how much of the chord is played: the triad, the sevenths, or every extension the chord has
Sets the register of the part, -24 to +24 semitones from middle C, which is how a musician states register whatever key the chart is in
Sets how long each note lasts as a percentage of its step; below 100% the notes are separated, at it they meet, above it they overlap
Chooses how loud each note is relative to the others: all the same, rising, falling, random, or first loudest
Bends each note after it has started, -2 to +2 semitones, and nought is off

inputs.text: Takes the note stream carrying the chord to play over

outputs.text: Carries the arpeggiated notes on as an MPX stream

notes: mpx IN takes a note stream from the mpx OUT of another DreamerMPX module, and the module does nothing until one is patched there
mpx OUT carries a note stream, not a voltage; patch it to another DreamerMPX module's mpx IN, or to fromMPX where ordinary voltages are wanted
up to four MPX cables can be patched into the one MPX input, and the notes arriving on them are merged
a cable between two MPX jacks turns pink once it has taken; a cable from an MPX jack to anything else keeps its ordinary colour and carries nothing
there is no clock input here; the beat is read from the MPX stream, so the chart or progression upstream sets the tempo
the chord and the beat both come from the MPX stream patched in, and only mpxChart and mpxProgression put harmony on a stream, so nothing sounds until one of those reaches this input
an MPX cable carries a note stream rather than a voltage and goes to an MPX input; fromMPX turns a stream back into gates and pitch for the wider rack
